A four-band graph of the 28-day menstrual cycle sharing one horizontal axis. Top band: pituitary hormones, with an FSH line (soft blue) rising early then low, and an LH line (orange) with a sharp spike at day 14. Second band: ovary events drawn as small pictures left to right: a small follicle, a growing follicle, a large mature follicle bursting and releasing an egg at day 14, then a corpus luteum growing and then shrinking. Third band: ovarian hormones, an oestrogen line (pink) peaking just before day 14 with a smaller second rise later, and a progesterone line (purple) low in the first half and high from day 15 to about day 24 then falling. Bottom band: the thickness of the uterus lining as a red-pink shaded area, thin and shedding on days 1 to 5, thickening on days 6 to 14, thickest on days 15 to 28.

Side view (longitudinal section) of the human male reproductive system and nearby organs. Show the urinary bladder at the top, the two seminal vesicles behind the bladder, the prostate gland below the bladder surrounding the start of the urethra, a small bulbourethral (Cowper's) gland below the prostate, the urethra running through the penis to the opening at the tip, erectile tissue inside the penis, the scrotum hanging outside the body containing one testis with the coiled epididymis on its back, and the sperm duct (vas deferens) looping up from the epididymis over the bladder to join the urethra through the ejaculatory duct. Also show the ureter coming down to the bladder and the rectum and backbone outline faintly behind. Soft pastel colours: pale blue ducts, light pink organs, yellow glands.

Two cells drawn side by side but not to scale. Left: a human sperm cell drawn large and horizontally, with an oval head containing a nucleus, a cap-like acrosome at the front, a middle piece with spiral mitochondria, and a long thin tail. Right: a human egg cell (secondary oocyte) as a large round cell with a central nucleus, granular cytoplasm with tiny yolk droplets, the cell membrane, a clear thick layer (zona pellucida) around it, and an outer ring of small follicle cells (corona radiata). Labels on sperm: acrosome, head, nucleus, middle piece, mitochondria, tail (flagellum). Labels on egg: corona radiata (follicle cells), zona pellucida (jelly coat), cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, yolk droplets. Add the note "not to scale" under the two cells. Soft blue sperm, peach-coloured egg.

Front view of the human female reproductive system. Show the uterus in the centre as a pear-shaped muscular organ cut open to reveal its thick muscular wall and inner lining, a Fallopian tube (oviduct) curving out from each top corner of the uterus and ending in a funnel with finger-like fimbriae, an oval ovary close to each funnel (one ovary cut open to show follicles at different stages and a released egg), the narrow neck of the uterus (cervix) at the bottom, and the vagina below opening to the outside. Soft pink and peach colours.

Sequence of four panels showing fertilisation. Panel 1: many small sperm swimming around a large round egg with its outer corona radiata of follicle cells and clear zona pellucida. Panel 2: close-up of one sperm head at the zona pellucida, with its acrosome releasing enzymes (shown as small dots) digesting a path. Panel 3: the sperm head entering the egg cytoplasm, with the zona pellucida thickening into a fertilisation membrane and other sperm blocked outside. Panel 4: the male and female nuclei meeting and fusing in the centre to form the zygote nucleus, with a small polar body at the edge. Panel titles: 1 sperm reach egg, 2 acrosome reaction, 3 one sperm enters, 4 nuclei fuse. Soft blue sperm, peach egg, purple nuclei.

Front-view diagram of the female reproductive tract showing the journey from ovulation to implantation. On the right, an ovary releasing an egg into the funnel of the oviduct; along the oviduct, a numbered sequence of small drawings: fertilisation (sperm meeting egg) in the upper third of the oviduct, the zygote, 2-cell stage, 4-cell stage, 8-cell stage, morula (solid ball), then entering the uterus as a blastocyst (hollow ball with an inner cell mass), and finally the blastocyst embedding in the thick endometrium on the uterine wall. Soft pink tract with lilac embryos.

A numbered flow diagram of IVF in six steps arranged left to right in two rows. 1. A woman receiving a hormone injection, with a small drawing of an ovary containing several large follicles. 2. Egg collection: a fine needle guided by an ultrasound probe through the vagina into an ovary, with eggs being drawn up. 3. A sperm sample in a small container, with sperm being washed in a tube. 4. A glass petri dish in which eggs are surrounded by sperm, inside an incubator. 5. A microscope view of an early embryo dividing (2-cell, 4-cell and 8-cell stages, then a blastocyst). 6. Embryo transfer: a thin catheter passed through the cervix placing an embryo in the uterus. Step titles: 1 stimulate ovaries, 2 collect eggs, 3 collect sperm, 4 fertilise in dish, 5 grow embryos, 6 transfer embryo. Soft pastel colours.

Longitudinal section of a pregnant uterus with a foetus about 6 months old, head downward, floating in the amniotic sac. Show the thick muscular uterine wall, the placenta attached to the upper uterine wall, the umbilical cord running from the placenta to the foetus's navel, the amnion enclosing amniotic fluid, the cervix with a mucus plug at the bottom, and the vagina below. Add a small inset enlargement of the placenta showing chorionic villi (from the foetus) projecting into spaces filled with the mother's blood, with umbilical artery and vein inside the villi, and arrows showing oxygen and food passing to the foetus and carbon dioxide and urea passing to the mother. Soft pink and peach colours with red and blue vessels.
